newsitem.title: UK: P&O Q3 figures show tough trading for ferries.
newsitem.headline: P&O Q3 figures show tough trading for ferries.

text.p: Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co Plc (P&O) said on Wednesday that its third quarter statistics showed European Ferry rates were still under pressure despite a smaller percentage drop in volumes than seen earlier this year.

Also, the container traffic division faced "a tough competitive environment with strong downward pressure on rates, particularly in the Far East to Europe trade," P&O said. This led to a fallback in average revnues.
The cruises unit was reported to be having a good year, however.
P&O said the European ferries business saw third-quarter passenger, tourist vehicle and freight carryings down 6.8 percent, 9.6 percent and 3.6 percent respectively on a year ago.
Tough competition from the Channel Tunnel led to P&O and Stena Line announcing a merger of their businesses on the cross channel ferry market on October 3 under a new joint venture.

The latest quarterly P&O figures also reported tough times for containers which saw average revenues for the third quarter fall back on the previous three months, reflecting poor Far East to Europe rates.
This problem is seen growing worse in the final quarter.

Cruises was more upbeat, with higher yields than last year and a good outlook for the remainder of the year and the start of 1997. In Princess cruises third quarter capacity rose 17 percent on 1995 due to the introduction of a new liner in December last year.
